correctness.rationale: For full-support iid alphabet, the Hoeffding decomposition gives exactly four nonnegative long-run variance terms: squared L2 norms of f1+f2+f3, f12+f23, f13, and f123, with edge corrections bounded in L2. Vanishing is equivalent pointwise to f=mu+h(a,b)-h(b,c), h=f1(a)-f3(b)+f12(a,b); the converse telescopes. For three ordered symbols the aab and abb equations give constant H_a−H_b over all a<b, and applying a<b<c forces it zero; bba then determines descending pair potentials. Hence precisely constants, ascent-difference U and descent-difference D in the thirteen supported coordinates for q≥3. On two symbols four independent edge-constant-coboundary scores survive among seven possible weak patterns, including W, and six forbidden coordinates give ten full nullities; q=1 is deterministic. Bounded stationary two-dependence gives the multivariate CLT and known-null pseudoinverse chi-square degrees 3/10. Separately implemented exact de Bruijn linear algebra checked q=1..5 and exact rational covariance matrices checked q=1..4; these are corroborative finite checks, not a proof of all q or probabilities.

value.rationale: Generalized weak-order pattern counts with ties are established nonparametric serial-dependence observables. Their full long-run covariance is systematically singular, and the exact effective degrees of freedom for a specified finite-alphabet iid null are needed to construct valid singular-covariance quadratic tests. The probability-independent 0/3/10 dimension jump and explicit additional binary telescoping contrast are a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or recomputation of a covariance table. The theorem does not claim nuisance-estimation-adjusted tests, dependent observations or variable/infinite alphabets; the calibration applies only to a specified null law.

limitations: Fixed positive iid finite ordered alphabet and overlapping length-three windows only; no higher patterns, dependent series, unknown-parameter chi-square calibration, or infinite support.
